newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia govt approves new unfair dismissal rules.
newsitem.headline: Australia govt approves new unfair dismissal rules.

text.p: Australian Industrial Relations Minister Peter Reith said on Wednesday the government had formally given the go-ahead for rules to start on July 1 that partially exempt small firms from unfair dismissal provisions.
Reith said that under the provisions of the Workplace Relations Act 1996 the partial exemption would encourage small companies to employ staff.
Under the regulations new employees who work in a firm with 15 staff or less are excluded from the Federal unfair dismissal provisions until they have been continually employed for a year.
Reith called on the Labor opposition to support the legislation in Parliament's upper house, the Senate, where the government does not hold a majority.
Decision time for Labor could be May 14 or September 24 at the latest, he said in a statement.
The formal go-ahead had been granted by the executive council, a formal meeting of the cabinet with Governor-General Sir William Deane that approves executive actions.
